turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip said that Nikhil's threats were as predictable as the rain in summer.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil informed Sandip that he was not making threats, but stating facts, and that Sandip's actions were a direct threat to his people.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala watched the exchange with interest, her eyes darting between Sandip and Nikhil.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was so scared of his own shadow that he had to rely on the fear of others.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil retorted that Sandip's mockery only showed his own lack of understanding of the situation.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala's expression remained calm, but her brow furrowed slightly as she listened to Sandip's words.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip said that Nikhil was only trying to save his own skin, and that he would not be intimidated.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil explained that his actions were not driven by self-preservation, but by a sense of duty to his people.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala's gaze shifted to Sandip's followers, who were watching the exchange with growing unease.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was trying to provoke him into making a move, but Nikhil would never take the bait.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil stated that he would not be provoked, and that he would take all necessary measures to protect his people.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala's eyes narrowed slightly as she considered Nikhil's words.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip said that Nikhil's people were already fleeing, and that he would soon be left with nothing.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil countered that his people were not fleeing, but preparing to defend themselves.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala's expression turned thoughtful as she listened to Sandip's boasts.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was the one who was afraid, and that he was trying to hide it.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil stated that he was not afraid, and that he would stand by his people no matter what.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala's eyes flicked back to Nikhil, who was standing tall despite Sandip's jibes.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip said that Nikhil was a coward, and that he would never be able to protect his people.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil looked at Sandip with a mixture of sadness and determination, and said that he would do everything in his power to protect his people, even if it meant standing alone.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
